blocks.text: The perfect Bondi shakeout run is short, flat and gentle — 20 to 30 easy minutes along the promenade the morning before your race, never a hard effort. I've watched hundreds of visiting runners do exactly this in the days before the Sydney Marathon, and the ones who get it right treat it as a nerve-settler, not a training session. Here's how I'd do a pre-marathon jog in my own backyard.
The classic: the Bondi promenade out-and-back

If you only do one thing, run the beachfront promenade. It stretches from the North Bondi end down to the Icebergs end and back, hugging the sand the whole way. It's wide, flat and level — no stairs, no cambered road — exactly what you want when the goal is to loosen the legs without loading them. An easy out-and-back here lands you around 2 to 3 km, and you can turn back whenever your legs feel awake.

Because it's so flat and forgiving, it's the route I steer nervous first-timers toward. You're never far from a water bubbler, a bench or a toilet, and you'll almost always have other runners for company.

Go at first light. Sunrise over the water is genuinely spectacular, the promenade is quiet before the crowds arrive, and an early jog helps reset your body clock if you've flown in across time zones. Check the sunrise time for your date so you're lacing up as the sky starts to glow.
If you want a little more: a taste of the coastal walk

The Bondi to Bronte Coastal Walk is Sydney's most famous stretch of clifftop path, and you don't need to run the whole thing. A gentle jog to Tamarama and back gives you the ocean views and the sea air without committing your legs to the full distance — check Waverley Council for the exact route and length before you go.

blocks.title: Mind your footing the day before a race
blocks.text: This path has steps, narrow sections and uneven sandstone, and it gets busy with walkers stopping for photos — a recipe for a rolled ankle the day before you need your legs most. Keep the pace to a shuffle, give way to walkers, and drop back to the flat promenade if it's crowded.
Fuel, coffee and the golden rule

Bondi's café culture is part of the fun, and a flat white on the promenade after an easy jog is a lovely pre-race ritual. There are plenty of cafés along and just behind the beachfront, though I'd glance at current opening hours before you set out, since they change with the seasons.

The golden rule the day before a marathon: keep it familiar and keep it light. A shakeout isn't the morning to test a brand-new smoothie bowl or a triple-shot coffee your stomach has never met. Fuel gently, hydrate, and save the big feed for after you cross the line.
Why Bondi works so well for a shakeout

items: Flat by design — the promenade lets you keep the effort genuinely easy.
Scenic enough that 20 minutes flies by and your head clears.
Facilities on tap: bubblers, toilets, benches and cafés close at hand.
A built-in running community — you'll pass plenty of fellow runners at dawn.

blocks.title: One thing to plan for
blocks.text: The Sydney Marathon doesn't start or finish at Bondi — it runs across the Harbour Bridge and finishes near the Opera House. If you're basing yourself in Bondi, sort out your race-morning transport in advance and confirm the start time and logistics on the official TCS Sydney Marathon website.

items.q: How long should a pre-marathon shakeout run be?
items.a: Short and easy — most runners keep it to around 20 to 30 minutes at a relaxed, conversational pace, roughly 2 to 4 km. The aim is to wake the legs and settle the nerves, not build fitness. If in doubt, do less.

items.q: Where's the best place to run in Bondi the day before a race?
items.a: The flat beachfront promenade from the North Bondi end to the Icebergs end and back. It's level, wide and free of stairs — the gentlest option for tired-legs-to-be. If you want ocean views, jog a short section of the coastal path toward Tamarama and turn back.

items.q: When should I do my Bondi shakeout run?
items.a: First thing in the morning. It's cooler, quieter and the sunrise over the water is unbeatable — and an early run helps reset your body clock if you've travelled across time zones. Check the day's sunrise time so you're out as it gets light.

items.q: Does the Sydney Marathon start at Bondi Beach?
items.a: No. The course crosses the Sydney Harbour Bridge and finishes near the Opera House, not at Bondi. If you're staying in Bondi, plan your race-morning transport ahead and confirm timings on the official TCS Sydney Marathon site.

items.q: What should I eat or drink before a shakeout run?
items.a: Keep it familiar and light — a small, plain breakfast you've had before, plus water. Save experiments and heavy meals for after the race. A post-run coffee is a fine reward, just don't overdo it the day before.

blocks.text: That's the whole secret: keep it short, keep it easy, and let Bondi do the rest. Breathe in the salt air, let the sunrise settle your nerves, and jog home fresh and ready. Rest up — the hard work is tomorrow.
